text.p: The Dutch dropped their first points of the World Cup campaign when they were beaten 1-0 by Turkey in their European group seven qualifier on Wednesday.
Hakan Sukur headed the only goal past a helpless Edwin van der Sar in the 52nd minute after breaking free from his marker and meeting defender Ilker Yagcioglu's cross.
The Netherlands had a chance to equalise in the 86th minute when they were awarded a penalty after Alpay Ozalan brought down Pierre Van Hooijdonk on the edge of the area.
But Clarence Seedorf skied the ball over the bar to the relief of most of the 20,000 fans.
Ecstatic Turkey coach Mustafa Denizli said: "We have given the people of this country such happiness, we have beaten these giants. There can be no greater joy than this."
Dutch coach Guus Hiddink was magnanimous in defeat. "Turkey fought really well," he said. " The best team won on the day."
The Dutch lead the group with 12 points from five games, with the Belgians three points behind with a match in hand. Turkey go third with seven points from four games.
The Netherlands dominated the first half with Patrick Kluivert and Seedorf showing their class up front Aron Winter and Arthur Numan exposing the Turkish defence with fine crosses.

Turkey looked a different team after the boost of Hakan's goal. Goalkeeper Rustu Recber started intercepting crosses which had left him dangerously exposed in the first half and his defence worked with added spirit.

Turkey - 1-Rustu Recber, 2-Ilker Yagcioglu, 3-Bulent Korkmaz, 4-Tolunay Kafkas (16-Tayfur Havutcu 80), 5-Alpay Ozalan, 6-Abdullah Ercan (14-Oguz Cetin 88), 7-Tayfun Korkut, 8-Ogun Temizkanoglu, 9-Hakan Sukur, 10-Tugay Kerimoglu, 11-Celil Sagir.

Netherlands - 1-Edwin van der Sar, 2-Micael Reiziger (12-Marc Overmars 80), 3-Jaap Stam, 4-Frank de Boer, 5-Arthleftur Numan, 6-Witti Jonk, 7-Aron Winter (17-Pierre van Hooijdonk 66), 8-Ronald de Boer, 9-Patrick Kluivert, 10-Clarence Seedorf, 11-Phillip Cocu.
